hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 127.0722 mi; paid miles 127 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Seward Highway mileposts; Anchorage–Seward is approximately 126–127 paid miles, represented as 127. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

state_miles.source: derived 2026-11-05: the leg's archived route geometry intersected with OpenStreetMap state and province boundary relations (boundary=administrative, admin_level=4); at_mi = cumulative geometry distance at each boundary crossing, rescaled to leg miles; state miles = differences of those boundaries. OpenStreetMap, boundary relations read from the OpenStreetMap API on 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 148.0890 mi; paid miles 147 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway to Tern Lake plus Sterling Highway to Soldotna, approximately 90+57=147 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: mountainous
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

stops.source: Position and diesel read from OSM node 410734041 (fuel:diesel=yes), OpenStreetMap planet extract 2026-11-16. checkpoints.source: Read: Livengood from OpenStreetMap node 150921772 (place=hamlet), planet file of 2026-11-16, named as in BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide. Derived: at_mi is the nearest point of the leg's archived route, 1.7 mi from that point, measured along the route.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 253.6685 mi; paid miles 259 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Livengood/Dalton MP 0 is 84 miles north of Fairbanks and Coldfoot is MP 175; derived paid miles 84+175=259. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

state_miles.source: derived 2026-11-05: the leg's archived route geometry intersected with OpenStreetMap state and province boundary relations (boundary=administrative, admin_level=4); at_mi = cumulative geometry distance at each boundary crossing, rescaled to leg miles; state miles = differences of those boundaries. hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: mountainous
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 150.7879 mi; paid miles 151 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts, approximately MP 115 at Glennallen to MP 266 at Delta Junction; derived as 266−115=151. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 253.6889 mi; paid miles 259 from mileposts: BLM Alaska 2024 Dalton Highway Visitor Guide: Livengood/Dalton MP 0 is 84 miles north of Fairbanks and Coldfoot is MP 175; derived paid miles 84+175=259. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. BLM describes the Dalton as mostly gravel; separate gravel-surface gameplay is not modeled. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 117.7467 mi; paid miles 115 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Richardson Highway mileposts, MP 0 at Valdez to approximately MP 115 at Glennallen; derived as 115−0=115. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 74.7071 mi; paid miles 75 from mileposts: The MILEPOST and Bell's Alaska Highway logs place Homer in town near MP 173, not at the MP 179.5 end of the Spit; Soldotna is around MP 94–96. The city-pin drive is about 75 miles, with router distance recorded separately. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 127.0468 mi; paid miles 127 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Seward Highway mileposts; Anchorage–Seward is approximately 126–127 paid miles, represented as 127. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 93.7667 mi; paid miles 94 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway MP 0 to Tern Lake MP 37, then approximately 57 miles on Sterling Highway to Soldotna; derived paid miles 37+57=94. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 148.0699 mi; paid miles 147 from mileposts: The MILEPOST junction mileposts; Seward Highway to Tern Lake plus Sterling Highway to Soldotna, approximately 90+57=147 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 74.7109 mi; paid miles 75 from mileposts: The MILEPOST and Bell's Alaska Highway logs place Homer in town near MP 173, not at the MP 179.5 end of the Spit; Soldotna is around MP 94–96. The city-pin drive is about 75 miles, with router distance recorded separately. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

corridor.source: Development-time public Valhalla truck costing over OpenStreetMap (valhalla1.openstreetmap.de, loaded-semi options matching tools/reroute_leg.py), accessed 2026-10-07. Router-reported 107.5063 mi; paid miles 108 from mileposts: The MILEPOST Alaska Highway mileposts; Tok to Delta Junction is 108 paid miles. Route points and Open-Meteo elevation positions are sampled from the Valhalla shape and scaled to paid miles. The road is within Alaska; state miles are derived from the paid total. Overall terrain is derived from the dominant Open-Meteo grade-segment classifier. The two-lane, undivided summary is an assumed corridor-level default, not a claim that every urban segment has only two lanes. The split Tok–Delta and Delta–Fairbanks paid-mile total is 204, two miles above the retired 202-mile composite; the residual is preserved, not redistributed. Where no posted OSM speed sample exists, 55 mph is explicitly assumed under 13 AAC 02.275. Unverified truck parking and capacity are not claimed.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: DERIVED, not read: Canada has no national inventory like HPMS, so the class is the terrain the leg's own grade profile spends the most miles in (the reroute-enrich rule: sustained grade of 5 percent, or 4 percent with 1,000 ft of relief within 5 miles, is mountain; 1.5 percent or 400 ft of relief is hills; else flat), mapped flat to level, hills to rolling and mountain to mountainous. It reads the same elevation as the grade, so it is no independent check on it.

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: rolling
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.

state_miles.source: derived 2026-11-05: the leg's archived route geometry intersected with OpenStreetMap state and province boundary relations (boundary=administrative, admin_level=4); at_mi = cumulative geometry distance at each boundary crossing, rescaled to leg miles; state miles = differences of those boundaries. OpenStreetMap, boundary relations read from the OpenStreetMap API on 2026-11-16: https://www.openstreetmap.org/.

speed_limits.source: OpenStreetMap maxspeed tags on the corridor highway ways, read from the Geofabrik extract of 2026-11-16 and matched within 90 m of the archived route; normalized to mph, maxspeed:hgv preferred where tagged.
Assumed 55 mph where no posted OpenStreetMap maxspeed way lies along the road in Alaska: the unposted default under 13 AAC 02.275.

hpms_terrain.name: level
hpms_terrain.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Terrain_Type, read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view). The class is HPMS's own; DERIVED here only in that one value stands for a whole leg -- the modal class over the HPMS sections intersecting the leg's bounding box, since HPMS classifies sections and a leg crosses many. Accessed 2026-11-22: https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms.cfm

meta.source: FHWA Highway Performance Monitoring System (HPMS) Surface_Type (Item 49) and Structure_Type (Item 4), codes per the HPMS Field Manual, Chapter 4 (https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/policyinformation/hpms/fieldmanual/page06.cfm and page04.cfm), read from the national ArcGIS Living Atlas layer (Federal User Community hpms_v2_view), accessed 2026-11-22. The class and the structure are READ. Mileage is DERIVED: each section's longest geometry piece projected onto the archived leg road and rescaled to the leg's miles, read in 0.005-mile bins, the highest functional class nearest the road winning where rows overlap. A run marked inventory_side is ASSUMED: the leg drives the non-inventory carriageway there, which HPMS gives no surface of its own, and the inventory carriageway's reading within 250 m is applied to it (meta inventory_share_* gives how much of the leg). A structure's hpms_mi is READ: the milepoint length of the HPMS sections behind it, each once. mile_scale is leg miles per measured mile of the archived road. Each surface entry reads 'from_mi to_mi class', then forward or reverse when it holds one way only, then iri=, faulting= and inventory_side where they apply; each structure reads 'from_mi to_mi kind', the way, then hpms= (its HPMS length). iri (inches per mile) and faulting (inches) are DERIVED: the mean of the section readings inside the run. Where HPMS has no reading nothing is written. HPMS reports bridge-sized culverts as bridges.
